investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-28T17:35–17:43Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for 126–147 seconds until the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, no agent VM was provisioned and the eval produced zero evidence, violating all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry the correct node affinity label. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that the resource pool is at capacity and no preemption victim exists. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: because the pod never reached a running state, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1883–1885) could not complete createAgent() and therefore produced no evidence, causing the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) to report all four required fields as missing.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on both eligible nodes, leaving zero schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, concentrating all scheduling pressure on those 2 nodes and making the cluster more vulnerable to capacity exhaustion.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user-created agents were not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs), their VM resource reservations may still be counted against the node's allocatable capacity.
Lower confidence — concurrent load from other workloads or eval runs consuming the same kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two eligible nodes at the time of the run.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-28T17:38–17:43Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm; 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), and preemption cannot help. Because the eval probe calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) and that agent pod never becomes schedulable, the probe times out without ever writing the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing the expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label. Of the remaining 4 nodes, none satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. The eval probe for remote-agent-state (and its siblings remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime) each attempt to provision a remote agent pod; all three fail before any evidence can be collected, so the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is entirely unmet. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes are not labeled or tainted to accept remote-agent pods, so even if VM capacity existed elsewhere the pods could not land there. This compounds the capacity problem.

TERTIARY — a recent increase in concurrent remote-agent workloads (e.g., from other users or automated jobs) may have consumed the finite kata.peerpods.io/vm quota before the eval probes ran, but no workload-traffic evidence is present to confirm this.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-28T17:35–17:43Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for 126–147 seconds until the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, no agent VM was provisioned and the eval produced zero evidence, violating all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry the correct node affinity label. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that the resource pool is at capacity and no preemption victim exists. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: because the pod never reached a running state, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1883–1885) could not complete createAgent() and therefore produced no evidence, causing the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) to report all four required fields as missing.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod is unscheduled

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on both eligible nodes, leaving zero schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, concentrating all scheduling pressure on those 2 nodes and making the cluster more vulnerable to capacity exhaustion.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user-created agents were not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs), their VM resource reservations may still be counted against the node's allocatable capacity.
Lower confidence — concurrent load from other workloads or eval runs consuming the same kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two eligible nodes at the time of the run.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-28T17:38–17:43Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm; 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), and preemption cannot help. Because the eval probe calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) and that agent pod never becomes schedulable, the probe times out without ever writing the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing the expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label. Of the remaining 4 nodes, none satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. The eval probe for remote-agent-state (and its siblings remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime) each attempt to provision a remote agent pod; all three fail before any evidence can be collected, so the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is entirely unmet. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-28 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place the eval pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never reached the createAgent call, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent eval environment has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every pod that requires a peer-pod VM slot is stuck in Unschedulable state indefinitely. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents the eval runner from provisioning any remote agent, making all downstream evidence collection and contract assertions impossible. This is an eval/observability infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the peer-pod VM resource have no remaining allocatable slots, and no preemption victims exist to free them. All three remote-agent checks share this failure mode simultaneously.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the eval pod's node affinity or node selector requires a label (e.g., a kata/peer-pod capable label) that only the 2 exhausted nodes carry, so the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of resource availability.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or production workloads are competing for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on only 2 nodes, transient exhaustion during the eval window is expected without additional node capacity.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check the current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 eligible nodes using kubectl describe nodes to determine if the cluster is still exhausted.
Identify and, if appropriate, drain or evict any non-critical pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots to restore scheduling headroom for remote-agent eval pods.

Assess whether the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have sufficient total capacity for concurrent eval runs plus any production workloads sharing the same resource; if not, provision additional peer-pod-capable nodes.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods to confirm whether the 4 non-matching nodes could be made eligible (e.g., by adding the required label) as a capacity expansion option.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (non-zero) kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion would not be the cause and a different scheduling constraint would need investigation.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded and produced all 5 required evidence keys, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the 4 non-matching nodes were found to carry the required node label/affinity at the time of the failure, the affinity mismatch explanation would be disproved and only the resource exhaustion on 2 nodes would remain.
If the eval runner logs showed the pod was scheduled but the agent process itself crashed or returned an unexpected response, the root cause would shift from scheduling to agent runtime behavior.

If no other workloads or pods were consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time, the exhaustion hypothesis would require re-examination of the node's total allocatable quantity vs. the pod's resource request.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-node-capacity) that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested counts on all eligible nodes and fails fast with a structured capacity-exhaustion message before attempting pod creation.

Add a scheduling pre-flight step within the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime eval probes that detects Unschedulable pod events within a short timeout (e.g., 30s) and returns a structured INFRA_ERROR status with the scheduler reason, enabling faster triage without waiting for the full outageLatencyMs timeout.

Add a sibling-correlation eval that fires when two or more remote-agent checks share the same Unschedulable scheduler message within the same run window, automatically tagging the failure as a shared infrastructure dependency rather than independent check failures.
Add a historical baseline eval that tracks kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization over time so capacity exhaustion trends can be detected before they cause eval failures.
